newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares jump 4.93 pct in strong mrng activity.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares jump 4.93 pct in strong mrng activity.

text.p: Istanbul shares soared in heavy volume on Friday morning amid growing hopes that a planned secularist alliance would win a confidence vote in parliament in coming weeks, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed up 84 points, or 4.93 percent at 1,789 after brushing an all-time trading high of 1,794 in the session.
Morning volume more than tripled to 28.69 trillion lira from Thursday's 8.14 trillion.

Brokers said the resignations of four MPs from the ruling Islamist-led coalition parties buoyed Prime Minister Designate Mesut Yilmaz's chances of winning a confidence vote in his planned alliance excluding the Islamist Welfare Party (RP).
Three deputies from the junior coalition party True Path Party (DYP) and one from the RP quit their parties this morning.

"The market began an upward move yesterday on Yilmaz's remarks that the President would approve his coalition. The resignations further boosted morale in the market," Toygar Sungur from Meksa securities.
"The new index targets will be 1,850 and then 2,000 points if the resignations continue and Yilmaz gets the vote," he said.

The index had soared 8.04 percent to an record close of 1,774 on Monday on hopes that the secularist pact would be set up. But it dived 5.07 percent on Tuesday after True Path leader Tansu Ciller refused to discuss Yilmaz's offer to join his alliance.
Yilmaz has said he would present his cabinet list to President Suleyman Demirel early next week.

He has won the support of two left-wing parties, a small right-wing grouping and conservative independent MPs. With the latest resignations, the number of MPs expected to back Yilmaz rose to 272, compared with 275 deputies supporting the Islamists and their allies.

Of the 243 shares traded, 221 rose and only eight fell while 14 finished steady. The IMKB Industrial jumped 4.54 percent to 1,682, the IMKB Services leapt 4.38 percent to 1,833 and the IMKB Financial soared 4.91 percent to 1,900.

The most heavily traded shares were again bluechips -- largely state-owned flat steel maker Eregli, up 1,250 lira at 24,500 and petroleum products marketer Petrol Ofisi, up 1,750 lira at 28,000 and utilities Cukurova Elektrik, up 12,500 lira at 255,000 and Aktas Elektrik, up 10,000 lira at 242,500.
